strings.title: MonkeyThrive — Offline Nervous System Regulation
strings.description: A free, 100% offline, zero-telemetry nervous system regulation toolkit for trauma recovery, CPTSD grounding, and physiological sighs. No guilt mechanics.
strings.ogDescription: A free, zero-telemetry nervous system regulation toolkit for trauma recovery and CPTSD grounding. 100% offline. No tracking, no guilt mechanics.
strings.jsonLdDescription: A free, 100% offline, zero-telemetry nervous system regulation toolkit for trauma recovery, CPTSD grounding, and physiological sighs. No guilt mechanics. It does not replace professional care.
strings.newLede: No account and no streak around them. The work stays on the device.
strings.newAttuneBody: The tone uses the key of the Vivaldi season that is playing, so the pitch and the recording agree. Spring is E, Summer is G, and Autumn and Winter are F. The beat is a pulse you choose. It does not place you in a state.
strings.newHapticBody: Box breathing, the physiological sigh, and, when the reading is present, 4-7-8 can be followed with your eyes closed. The phone vibrates with the count. The vibration can be turned off.
strings.newDoseBody: Attune counts listening time on the device for that day. The recommendation is 45 minutes, enough for all four seasons. Past that, it asks before another session. You can continue.
strings.newOfflineBody: The journal is AES-256 sealed on this device. There is no account, no telemetry, and no subscription. The Android release is about 94 MB and has no network permission.
strings.devlogBody: A devlog of the Attune tones. The pitch follows the Vivaldi season. A long listen can leave you drowsy. The sound does not place you in a state.
strings.communityTitle: The project has a public trail.
strings.heroTitle: Offline regulation, in your own hands.
strings.heroLede: MonkeyThrive is a privacy-first toolkit for breathing, grounding, vagal cues, and bilateral stimulation. The name is a nod to Sun Wukong, the Monkey King: a restless mind can be trained, and strength becomes protective once it learns discipline.
strings.trust: Zero network. No account. No telemetry. Nothing you enter leaves the device.
strings.apkTrail: for a phone without an app store.
strings.packsLede: Extra music stays out of the app file.
strings.heroAlt: Sun Wukong in red and gold, holding a phone.
strings.whatTitle: Practices for the nervous system, kept on this device.
strings.whatBody1: MonkeyThrive is a small set of tools: paced breathing, a physiological sigh, cold water, sensory grounding, vagal cues, and bilateral stimulation. It runs in the browser and as a standalone Android app. The release build is made to work with no network permission.
strings.whatBody2: You start with a body map. Head, throat, chest, and stomach can be marked tight or heavy. The app shows that reading as overwhelmed, present, or flat or numb, and you see it before you continue. An empty map does not count as present. You are the authority on your own experience. The reading is not a diagnosis.
strings.whatBody3: The Monkey King stays in the name: self-made strength that learns a limit. In the app, that limit is practical. A tool that needs more capacity than the moment can hold stays closed.
strings.whyTitle: Built to be left alone, and easy to leave.
strings.whyOfflineBody: The release app has no network permission. Check-ins, journal entries, and readings stay on the device. There is no telemetry, no crash reporting, and no analytics.
strings.whyGatedBody: Window of Tolerance rules decide which tools open. The lock is the same for overwhelmed and for flat or numb. The rules are fixed. They are not a score, and they are not a diagnosis.
strings.whyGuiltBody: No streaks, no accounts, and no engagement algorithms. There is no score for the days you were away. The app is built to be easy to put down.
strings.whySourceBody: The source is public under GPL-3.0. The offline claim, the gates, and the crisis directory can be read in the repository.
strings.whoTitle: For people who want the tool, and nothing around it.
strings.who1: Trauma survivors who want regulation practice that stays on the device.
strings.who2: People who want no account, no telemetry, and no profile.
strings.who3: People on de-Googled Android, including GrapheneOS, CalyxOS, and Sailfish OS.
strings.who4: Anyone who wants a small set of practices without a wellness platform around them.
strings.toolsTitle: Some tools wait until the reading is present.
strings.toolsIntro: A check-in comes first. The same higher-intensity tools stay closed when the reading is overwhelmed and when it is flat or numb. Present is the only reading that opens them.
strings.toolBoxBody: A steady count you can follow.
strings.toolSighBody: Two inhales and a long exhale.
strings.toolColdBody: A short timer for the diving reflex.
strings.toolGroundBody: Name what you can sense around you.
strings.toolVagalBody: Humming, gargling, or a longer exhale.
strings.toolAnchorBody: The simplest screen, on the bar. On Android, the volume keys open it. Words stay off for the first few breaths.
strings.tool478Body: A longer pattern. Open when the reading is present.
strings.toolWimBody: Open when the reading is present, after the safety confirmations for that session.
strings.toolSafeBody: A visualisation stored on this device. Open when the reading is present.
strings.toolBilateralBody: For grounding and attention. It is not EMDR. It also waits until earlier parts of the app have been used, and it still requires a present reading.
strings.safetyTitle: A tool can sit with you. A person can help.
strings.safetyNowBody: The app includes an offline crisis directory, kept on the device and listed by country. You can also contact local emergency services directly. A call or text from that directory uses your phone’s own dialer or messages app.
strings.disclaimer: MonkeyThrive is a supportive self-regulation tool. It does not replace professional therapy, and it does not diagnose, assess, or treat any condition.
strings.footerLine: Built from lived experience. For everyone who is still here.
strings.safetyPageDescription: What MonkeyThrive is, what it refuses to do, and where to find a person.
strings.safetyLead: Plain limits for a tool that stays on your device.
strings.safetyWhat: MonkeyThrive is a supportive self-regulation tool. It does not replace professional therapy. It does not diagnose, assess, or treat any condition.
strings.safetyWot1: A check-in asks how you are right now. Higher-intensity tools stay closed when that check-in is outside a regulated state. The gates are fixed rules in the app. They are not a score, and they are not a diagnosis.
strings.safetyWot2: Bilateral cueing is for grounding and attention. It is not EMDR and it is not trauma reprocessing. Wim Hof-style breathing asks for safety confirmations at the start of each session.
strings.safetyWontH: What the app will not do
strings.safetyWont: There is no account, no streak, and no engagement ranking. The app does not send journal entries, check-ins, or sensor readings anywhere. The country you pick in the crisis directory stays in local storage.
strings.safetyNote: Need immediate human support? MonkeyThrive includes an offline crisis directory, or reach out to local emergency services directly.
